```python
# filename: compute_em_growth.py
funds = [
    {"name": "Fidelity Emerging Markets Index Fund", "ticker": "FPADX", "nav_2019": 12.50, "nav_2024": 15.00, "fee": "$0"},
    {"name": "Fidelity Emerging Markets Fund", "ticker": "FEMKX", "nav_2019": 28.40, "nav_2024": 32.50, "fee": "$0"},
    {"name": "Fidelity Emerging Asia Fund", "ticker": "FSEAX", "nav_2019": 30.10, "nav_2024": 32.00, "fee": "$0"},
    {"name": "Fidelity Global Emerging Markets Fund", "ticker": "FGEMX", "nav_2019": 10.00, "nav_2024": 11.50, "fee": "$0"},
]

# Compute percentage increases
for f in funds:
    pct = ((f["nav_2024"] - f["nav_2019"]) / f["nav_2019"]) * 100.0
    f["pct_increase"] = pct

# Identify lowest percentage increase
lowest = min(funds, key=lambda x: x["pct_increase"]) 

# Print results
print("Fund | Ticker | NAV May 2019 | NAV May 2024 | % Increase | Fee")
for f in funds:
    print(f"{f['name']} | {f['ticker']} | {f['nav_2019']:.2f} | {f['nav_2024']:.2f} | {f['pct_increase']:.2f}% | {f['fee']}")
print("\nLowest % increase:")
print(f"{lowest['name']} ({lowest['ticker']}) -> {lowest['pct_increase']:.2f}%")
```
